short_title: Why the foam forms and why it is so polluted (2024)
title: Unveiling the organic nature of phosphogypsum foam: Insights into formation dynamics, pollution load, and contribution to marine pollution in the Southern Mediterranean Sea
summary: Shows the foam is man-made and short-lived, held together by organic compounds and gypsum crystals. Those compounds explain why it holds so much pollution, and the foam carries and spreads phosphogypsum pollution in the sea.

findings.headline: The foam is man-made, short-lived and held together by organic compounds
findings.summary: The authors describe the foam as unnatural and short-lived, held together by soap-like organic compounds. These compounds explain why it holds so much pollution.
findings.headline_original: Foam is artificial, short-lived and stabilised by organic compounds
findings.summary_original: The foam is described as an unnatural, surfactant-stabilised, ephemeral aqueous foam whose organic nature explains its high contaminant load.

summary_original: Shows the foam is an artificial, short-lived foam stabilised by organic compounds and gypsum crystals. Those compounds explain its high contaminant load, and the foam carries and spreads phosphogypsum contaminants in the sea.
